title: Audit schema evolution roadmap: RBAC v2 impact and SIEM export guidance
summary: Working roadmap and tactical notes for evolving the audit/event schema from legacy v1 to intermediary v2 and full v3 delivery. Emphasis on RBAC v2 implications, dual-write strategies for migration, SIEM export normalization, and evidence automation hooks.
changelog: 2025-02-11: initial draft with high-level roadmap and RBAC v2 impact assessment
2025-02-20: added SIEM export normalization recommendations and compression notes
2025-03-04: appended evidence automation playbook and rollout checklist; set to in_review
content:
Purpose and scope:
This document captures a pragmatic evolution path for the platform audit/event schema across three delivery states (v1 legacy, v2 transitional, v3 target). Primary drivers: RBAC v2 release (role bindings and permission sets), customer SIEM expectations (normalized fields, denormalized actor context), and evidence automation required for compliance engagements. Intended audience: security, platform, SRE, product, and vendor/integration partners (SIEM/EDR).

High-level versioning strategy (goal):
- v1 (field set as-of 2023): sparse actor labels, legacy role strings, per-request token context.
- v2 (transitional): introduce explicit role_binding_id, actor_affinity, canonical_principal ids and dual-write compatibility headers. Backwards-compatible additions only; no breaking renames.
- v3 (target): normalized, typed schema with event lineage, deterministic event ids, trace sharding, and structured evidence attachments. v3 is the spec we want external customers and SIEM connectors to adopt long-term.

Key RBAC v2 impacts (what changes in audit events):
- actor representation: legacy events used "principal" freeform. v2 introduces canonical_principal (uuid) and actor_affinity (enum: service_account | user | system) to disambiguate cached tokens vs true actors.
- role metadata: add role_binding_id and role_graph_version to event context to link the effective permission set that allowed the action. This is critical for forensic reconstruction.
- permission resolution snapshot: events optionally include permission_snapshot_id when permission resolution occurred outside the default path (e.g., delegated roles).
- immutability: attach evidence_signature_id when an event is stored into the immutable audit bucket (for court/enterprise evidence).

Event taxonomy recommendations (categories):
- auth: login, token_refresh, session_revoke, grant_create, grant_delete
- policy: role_create, role_update, role_bind, permission_change
- config: config_change, secret_rotation, kms_key_attach
- runtime: model_infer_request, model_deploy, model_rollback, route_update
- data: blob_read, blob_write, secret_access, export_request
- system: node_reboot, autoscale_event, scheduler_preempt

Minimum v2 event envelope (text example, keep unchanged names when dual-writing):
- timestamp: RFC3339 UTC string
- event_id: v2-<opaque> (GUID)
- trace_id: request_trace id shared across services
- event_type: one of taxonomy categories above
- actor: { canonical_principal: "uuid", actor_affinity: "user|service_account|system", human_readable: "jane.doe@acme" }  -- note: store as a JSON string in logs until v3 rollout
- role_binding_id: optional string id of RBAC binding used to authorize
- permission_snapshot_id: optional string referencing the permission-resolution record
- resource: canonical resource id (type:name)
- outcome: success|failure|denied|unknown
- metadata: freeform map for event-specific fields (keep minimal in v2)
- retention_policy_tag: short tag for cross-team retention (e.g., "compliance:7y")

Compatibility and dual-write pattern:
- Dual-write mode: services emit both v1-style and v2-style events behind a feature flag. v2 fields should never remove v1 names; they should coexist. Example: emit principal and canonical_principal fields in the same envelope during migration.
- Headers for consumers: add X-Audit-Schema-Version: v2 and X-Audit-Compat: v1 to facilitate SIEM connectors deciding whether to normalize server-side.
- Consumer libraries: ship a normalization shim (go/python) that can convert v1/v2 envelopes into the v3 canonical format for downstream analytics and SIEM exports.

SIEM export normalization guidance (practical):
- flattening rules: map nested actor.{canonical_principal,actor_affinity,human_readable} -> actor_id, actor_type, actor_name. Avoid dots in field names for common SIEMs.
- timestamps: push RFC3339 with millisecond precision; if SIEM requires epoch_ms also include event_ts_ms field.
- event deduplication: include producer_id and event_seq when writing bursts from the same process. This reduces duplicate ingestion during retries.
- compression and delivery: recommend gzip over HTTPS for push-based exporters; chunk size capped at 5MB compressed or 10k events whichever comes first.
- schema header: include a compact header block at top of batch exports: schema_version=v2, producer=service-name, batch_id=uuid. This helps downstream parsers evolve without synchronous changes.

Evidence automation hooks (light playbook):
- on-demand evidence: a policy-triggered workflow will capture event + artifacts (config snapshot, role graph at t0, policy diff) and push to the immutable evidence service.
- evidence artifact naming: <evidence_type>/<service>/<resource>/<YYYYMMDD>/<evidence_uuid>.tar.gz
- signatures: evidence artifacts must be signed using customer KMS key when in Private deployment; hosted customers use Redwood HSM signing with audit_certificate_id attached to the event.
- retention & legal holds: evidence artifacts carry retention_policy_tag and a separate legal_hold boolean. The metadata must be queryable by compliance tooling.

Migration checklist (recommended rollout):
1) Finalize v2 schema draft and publish confluence spec.
2) Implement normalization shims in platform libs; release SDK minor version.
3) Opt-in dual-write behind org-level feature flag; run for 4–8 weeks.
4) Monitor parity metrics: actor mapping coverage, missing role_binding_id percent, permission_snapshot mismatch rate. Target <1% missing within two weeks for core services.
5) Engage top-10 SIEM customers with export samples; produce mapping tables and connector configs.
6) Cutover consumers: after parity thresholds met, flip producer-only v2 header and begin deprecating v1 producers on a rolling schedule.
7) Deliver v3 spec and migration tooling for final schema stabilization and consumer adoption.

Operational metrics to track during migration:
- percentage of events containing canonical_principal (goal: 99% within 2 weeks for API and console flows)
- role_binding_id coverage across policy-change events
- SIEM connector parsing errors per 10k events (goal: <5 per 10k)
- evidence_artifact_signing_failures (goal: 0)

Open questions / decisions for review:
- Should permission_snapshot be emitted synchronously or referenced by id with a background snapshot job? (performance vs forensic completeness tradeoff)
- Standardized name for actor_affinity enum values to share across SDKs and SIEMs. Proposal: user | service_account | system | impersonated
- Which export delivery patterns should Redwood support in hosted tier vs private deployments (push vs pull vs S3 export)?

Appendix: sample migration CLI snippets (illustrative)
- Enable dual-write for service: infra-cli audit-config set --service model-server --dual-write true --schema v2
- Run parity check (local): python tools/audit_parity_check.py --service model-server --days 7 --report parity-report.md
- Generate SIEM mapping artifact: node tools/siem-map-gen.js --schema v2 --output siem-mapping-model-server.json

Notes: This is a working doc. Expect changes after cross-team review (product/infra/customer-success/legal). The goal is to have a non-breaking, observable migration path that lets customers adopt richer audit semantics (RBAC v2 and evidence automation) without disrupting their downstream SIEM pipelines.
